title: An exact timing null did not resolve a concentration hierarchy beyond temporal power in eight mouse recordings
abstract: We tested temporal-power and response-alignment accounts of mouse visual response compression. We used 1,051 selected cells from eight distinct male mice in the Allen Visual Coding cohort and two movies. We derive an exact conditional timing null for a signal-concentration statistic from four disjoint repeat groups. Independent Fourier phases and independent circular shifts give the same expected second moment while preserving each cell's temporal cross-power and repeat-mean reliability. The null can be computed without neuron-pair matrices. Under fixed weights and independent repeat errors, its moment components have noise-unbiased estimates; their ratio is not unbiased. Simulations and real-array invariants validate the calculation. In 40 pooled mouse splits, attempted temporal-power matching reduced mean fitted alpha hierarchy slopes from 0.339 to 0.239 and from 0.303 to 0.198. Held-out power matching was poor, and one primary filter had gain 370, so these reductions do not quantify a biological fraction explained. In a declared post-result within-mouse test, excess concentration rose with hierarchy in 6–7 of 8 mice. Three of four mean mouse-bootstrap intervals excluded zero, but all Holm-adjusted sign tests were unresolved (p >=0.281), and unscaled movie three remained uncertain. The method gives a repeat-aware timing baseline. These data do not establish a stable hierarchy beyond temporal power or identify a circuit. Limits include eight convenience-selected male mice, unequal area coverage, scaling effects, finite-sample ratios and dependent repeat errors. Code, proof, aggregate evidence, figures and exact source checks are included; external cell-level data remain outside the bundle.
